entities.summary: Wojciech of Jastrzębiec was a Polish mediaeval politician and religious leader. A bishop of Cracow and Poznań, he also held prominent posts at the court of the king Władysław II of Poland.

entities.name: Wojciech Jastrzębiec
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wojciech Jastrzębiec (1362–1436) emerged as a preeminent Polish ecclesiastical and political figure during the late 14th and early 15th centuries, a period critical for the consolidation of the Jagiellonian dynasty and the Polish-Lithuanian Union. Born in Łubnice, he ascended through the ranks of the Polish church to become Archbishop of Gniezno, Primate of Poland, and concurrently held the influential positions of Bishop of Poznań and Bishop of Cracow. His career was intricately woven into the fabric of King Władysław II Jagiełło's court, where he served as Chancellor of the Crown, wielding significant influence over both domestic policy and foreign diplomacy, particularly in the ongoing struggle against the Teutonic Knights.

Jastrzębiec's career path commenced as Bishop of Poznań (1399–1412), followed by a pivotal tenure as Bishop of Cracow (1412–1423), the spiritual heart of the Polish kingdom. His appointment as Archbishop of Gniezno and Primate of Poland in 1423 solidified his status as the leading cleric in the realm. A key moment in his diplomatic career was his participation in the Council of Constance (1414–1418) as a prominent member of the Polish delegation. There, he staunchly supported Paul Włodkowic's arguments, advocating for the rights of pagan nations and challenging the Teutonic Order's theological justifications for their crusades against Lithuania, thus contributing to early discussions on international law and religious tolerance.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Wojciech Jastrzębiec's diplomatic efforts at the Council of Constance significantly shaped Poland's international standing and legal arguments against the Teutonic Knights. His influence helped stabilize the Jagiellonian dynasty during a critical period, ensuring the succession of Władysław III.
